paper_title: RLPlanner: Reinforcement Learning based Floorplanning for Chiplets with Fast Thermal Analysis

scenario.description: Selected scenario: the Ascend 910 System benchmark (ref [6]) in Table I, comparing RLPlanner, RLPlanner(RND), TAP-2.5D(HotSpot) and TAP-2.5D*(Fast Thermal Model). The RLPlanner row reports reward -7.4063, wirelength 18130 (labelled mm), temperature 77.12 C and runtime 7773 s. The paper mentions a github repository for the fast thermal model but gives no URL in the packet text, and the packet has no assets. Chiplet block names, x/y/width/height and per-block power values are not given in the 2-page paper, so no floorplan can be extracted from it.
scenario.architecture: 2.5D chiplet-based system on an interposer (Huawei Ascend 910 benchmark), floorplanned by RL (PPO with RND bonus) and TAP-2.5D baselines; thermal evaluation by HotSpot or a physics-informed fast thermal model (self- and mutual-thermal resistance tables)
scenario.operating_point: Maximum chiplet-system temperature in C (aggregation: maximum); the temperature limit T0 and the weights lambda, mu and alpha are not given. Total power is not given.

original_setup.solver: Fast physics-informed thermal model (LTI self- and mutual-thermal resistance tables characterized with HotSpot) used during RLPlanner training and evaluation. HotSpot is the ground-truth and baseline solver (TAP-2.5D(HotSpot)).
original_setup.optimizer: RLPlanner: reinforcement learning with proximal policy optimization (PPO) and an optional random network distillation (RND) exploration bonus. It jointly minimizes wirelength and maximum temperature. The baseline is the simulated-annealing-based TAP-2.5D.
original_setup.controller: None reported. The RL agent places chiplets sequentially at floorplanning time, with an action mask. There is no runtime thermal controller.
original_setup.benchmark: Ascend 910 System (ref [6]), Table I on PDF page 2. The RLPlanner row reports reward -7.4063, wirelength 18130 (column labelled mm), temperature 77.12 C and runtime 7773 s.

thermal_observable.location: Maximum operating temperature of the chiplet-based Ascend 910 system, taken from the RLPlanner row of Table I. The exact spatial location (which chiplet or grid cell) is not stated.
thermal_observable.aggregation: Maximum temperature over the system, as the fast thermal model estimates maximum chiplet-system temperature. The paper does not state whether it is a steady-state value. This is the single reported value for the RLPlanner row, not a mean over runs.

physical_mismatches.reason: 3D stacking is not modeled. The scenario is a 2.5D interposer-based chiplet floorplan, and the paper gives no stack or vertical-layer detail.

Interposer, package and material stack parameters (layer thicknesses, conductivities, TIM, heat spreader) are not given in the paper. The thermal result depends on them and cannot be reproduced without them.
Cooling and boundary conditions (heat sink, convection coefficient, ambient temperature) are not stated. The reported 77.12 C cannot be matched to any specific cooling configuration.

The paper reports only a steady-state-style maximum temperature, with no transient or workload-dependent thermal behavior. A transient or workload-driven Studio study would not correspond to the published observable.

The optimizer is PPO+RND reinforcement learning with a reward combining wirelength and a temperature penalty. A Studio simulation that does not reproduce this optimizer and reward cannot reproduce the published floorplan, so it can only evaluate a given floorplan.
The published temperature comes from the fast LTI thermal-resistance model approximating HotSpot (MAE 0.25 K), not a full-field solver. A different solver in Studio may give a different value.
No reliability or thermomechanical stress analysis is reported. The introduction mentions thermomechanical stress only as motivation.
